title: Sales enablement: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ethan Park
body:
Overview

This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's customer-facing sales enablement materials for engineering-led and enterprise buyers. It is intended for AE/SDR/solutions engineers and product marketing working on: positioning & messaging, competitive battle cards, pitch deck guidance, pricing guardrails, customer case study summaries, and a short security FAQ customized for prospects.

Use this page as the canonical source for:
- Core positioning statements for technical and executive audiences
- One-page competitive briefs and objection-handling language
- Recommended pitch-deck flow and slide-level talking points
- Pricing guidance and deal-structure examples for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
- Customer case study templates and anonymized examples to cite in sales motions
- A concise security FAQ to address early-stage prospect concerns

Ownership and distribution

- Owner: go-to-market (Product Marketing + Sales Enablement)
- Content owners: PMM (Product Marketing) maintains positioning and case studies; Solutions Engineering owns competitive briefs and pitch deck templates; Finance maintains pricing guidance; Security contributes to the FAQ and reviews any restricted items.
- Distribution: Link to this page from AE playbooks, demo kits, and the sales Slack channel (#sales-enable) and attach the latest pitch deck in the team drive.

1) Positioning & messaging

Short elevator (30s):
Redwood Inference is a production-first inference platform that makes running high-performance LLMs predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams reduce latency, lower per-token costs, and maintain reliability at scale with unified tooling and observability.

Value props (by buyer persona):
- Engineering/Platform lead:
  - Predictable latency and throughput across deployments; unified API and rollout controls reduce integration complexity.
  - Kernel selection, smart routing, and batching reduce CPU/GPU costs without code changes.
- Product/Feature lead:
  - Faster time-to-value with hosted API + consistent behavior when moving to Dedicated/Private.
  - Observability and quality guardrails prevent regressions and make model upgrades safe.
- Security/Compliance lead:
  - VPC/private control plane options, KMS/HSM integrations, and enterprise audit logging for regulated data.

Key messages to test (A/B):
- Message A (Cost-centric): "Lower your per-token inference cost by 30-60% using batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles while keeping latency SLOs."
- Message B (Reliability-centric): "Keep customer-facing features online with multi-tier fallbacks and SLA-backed Dedicated capacity."

Proof points / metrics to cite
- Typical per-token cost reductions customers see after optimization: 30-50% (internal benchmark suite).
- Median 95th-percentile latency on Redwood Dedicated for 8k-seq models: 120-220ms (model dependent).
- Customer example: a B2B SaaS company reduced inference spend by 42% after adopting Redwood batching + caching profiles.

2) Competitive briefs (one-page templates)

Structure (use for each competitor):
- Competitor name (e.g., CloudX AI endpoints)
- Who they win against / product strengths (short bullet list)
- Common prospect signals they use (e.g., managed model catalog, simple pricing)
- Our counter-positioning (concise bullets with proof points)
- Typical objections and recommended responses (scripts for AE/SE)
- Deal motion recommendations (when to involve SE, when to propose Dedicated trial)

Example: Competitive brief — Managed Cloud Endpoint Vendor
- Strengths: Broad model catalog, straightforward per-request pricing, quick start for prototypes.
- How they typically sell: rapid POC, developer demo, then migrate to committed capacity if usage grows.
- Redwood counter-positioning:
  - For production workflows: highlight our cost controls (batching, KV caching), unified rollout tools, and Dedicated pools with SLA.
  - For security-conscious customers: emphasize Private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations.
- Objection handling:
  - "Your platform is more complex than theirs": Response: "We provide self-serve defaults and quickstarts for dev/test while offering predictable Dedicated/Private options for production."

3) Pitch deck guidance (recommended flow and content)

Recommended 10-12 slide flow (ideal for technical buyers + GTM lead):
1. Title + one-line summary (elevator)
2. Customer problem (latency, cost, reliability) with data points
3. Redwood solution overview (hosting modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
4. How it works (runtime, smart routing, caching/batching) — one diagram
5. Product demo / screenshots (console, perf dashboards)
6. Key differentiators (production-first, unified runtime, cost controls)
7. Customer success snapshots (short case bullets)
8. Pricing and sizing guidance (example T-shirt sizes)
9. Security & compliance summary (audit logging, KMS, VPC)
10. Next steps / pilot proposal (trial scope, success metrics, timeline)

Slide-level talking points (examples):
- Slide 4 (How it works): "We orchestrate requests across runtime variants, selecting kernels and batching strategies optimized for each model and sequence length. This is how we reduce unit costs while maintaining tail latency."
- Slide 8 (Pricing and sizing): include a sample calculation (see Pricing Guidance) tailored to the prospect's expected qps and avg tokens per call.

Operational tips for SEs on calls
- Always start by aligning on the metric that matters: latency SLO or cost target.
- If the prospect references production scale, proactively propose a Dedicated proof-of-concept with target SLOs and a short-term capacity commit.
- Use the console to show token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboard in live demo.

4) Pricing guidance and deal structuring

Pricing model overview (high-level):
- Hosted API: Usage-based (per-token generation & embeddings increments), tiered add-ons for observability retention and premium SLA.
- Dedicated: Monthly/annual reserved capacity with optional burst and overage rates.
- Private: Platform license + deployment/support fee; pricing varies by deployment profile.

Deal sizing rules of thumb (T-shirt sizes):
- Small (Dev / Early POC): < $2k/month equivalent. Recommendation: Hosted, free credits, short-term trial (30 days).
- Medium (Pilot / Featured product): $2k-25k/month. Recommendation: Start hosted or small Dedicated pool, include observability add-on for pilot.
- Large (Enterprise / Production): > $25k/month. Recommendation: Dedicated or Private with a 12-24 month commit, SLA, and enterprise support.

Sample math for a mid-sized pilot
- Expectations: 5 qps average, 50 tokens per request, 30-day trial, 24/7 usage.
- Raw token volume: 5 qps * 50 tokens * 3600s * 24h * 30d ≈ 648M tokens.
- Pricing guidance: Use hosted per-token rate as baseline and propose Dedicated ROI: show expected reduction in per-token cost after batching and caching (conservative estimate 30% save).

Discounting & approvals
- Standard enterprise discounts require Sales Ops approval for > 20% off list price or multi-year pricing.
- Any customer data residency or security exceptions require Security and Legal review; include expected timeline in the proposal.

5) Case studies (templates + anonymized example)

Case study template (fill for each customer):
- Customer: [Company anonymized if requested]
- Industry / vertical:
- Problem statement: customer's pain points prior to Redwood
- Solution: Redwood deployment type, models used, key configuration (batching, KV caching, quantization)
- Outcome / metrics: latency improvement, cost savings, error-rate reduction, time-to-market reduction
- Owner / contact: AE and CSM

Anonymized example (short):
- Customer: Mid-market B2B SaaS (anonymized)
- Problem: High per-session latency and exploding inference cost as features scaled to customers.
- Solution: Migrated from per-request cloud endpoint to Redwood Dedicated; enabled continuous batching, prefix caching for common prompts, and model quantization profile.
- Outcome: 42% reduction in inference spend, 2x throughput improvement during peak load, consistent 95th-percentile latency under 300ms.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short, to use in early conversations)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted customers, data is stored in region-specific encrypted storage. For Dedicated and Private deployments, data remains in customer-owned environments (VPC/air-gapped) with optional on-prem packaging.

Q: How is customer data protected in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 encryption at rest. For Private deployments, we support HSM/KMS integrations for key control.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
A: Yes — Dedicated and Private customers can integrate their KMS/HSM for encryption keys.

Q: What audit capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs (API calls, admin actions) are available via the Console and can be exported to customer SIEM for Dedicated/Private deployments. Retention policies are configurable per contract.

Q: How do you handle model provenance and third-party model licensing?
A: We maintain a model catalog with provenance metadata and licensing notes. Security reviews include model license checks when requested by the customer.

Q: What is your incident response posture?
A: We publish an incident process and SLA-backed response times for Dedicated customers. Security incidents follow our security incident runbook and we provide timeline and remediation reports to impacted customers.

Q: Can we run an on-premises evaluation or air-gapped deployment?
A: Yes — we offer an on-prem package for qualified enterprise prospects; lead time varies based on environment validation.

Q: What certifications or compliance do you maintain?
A: Public hygiene: SOC 2 Type II (in process / applicable depending on product). For enterprise engagements, we supply evidence and work with customer security teams on controls and assessments.

Appendices and supporting artifacts

- Attachments to maintain in the team drive: latest pitch deck (master), competitive one-pagers, pricing calculator spreadsheet, case study slide pack, and the security FAQ pack (with redacted artifacts for demos).
- Reference pages: product roadmap, serving runtime release notes, eng-sre runbooks for incident escalations.

How to update this page

1. PMM owns messaging updates — update Positioning & messaging when features/differentiators change.
2. Solutions Engineering owns competitive briefs — update after loss reviews or competitive intel.
3. Finance owns pricing guidance — update annually or for major pricing model changes.
4. Security must review and sign off on any changes to the Security FAQ or confidential attachments.
